latest.title: New Convertible Loan Note Facility
latest.content:
Today 16:18
RNS Number : 0403L
Critical Metals PLC
03 July 2026
Critical Metals plc / EPIC: CRTM / Market: Main Market
3 July 2026
Critical Metals plc
("Critical Metals" or the "Company")
New Convertible Loan Note Facility
Critical Metals plc (LSE:CRTM), a mining company established to acquire mining opportunities in the critical and strategic metals sector, which operates the Molulu Copper/Cobalt Project ("Molulu") in the Democratic Republic of Congo, announces that it has agreed with NIU Invest SE ("NIU"), the Company's majority shareholder, that it will subscribe for £2,500,000 convertible loan notes under a new convertible loan note instrument ("CLN Instrument") on similar terms to the £2,100,000 convertible loan instrument that the Company created in December 2025 ("2025 CLN Instrument"). The Company has not issued all of notes under this instrument and the remaining notes will be subscribed for by NIU at par by the end of September 2026. The funds raised under the CLN Instrument and the 2025 CLN Instrument is intended to provide the Company with the capital it needs for at least the next 12 months and will be used to explore acquisition opportunities in the mining sector, fund exploration and/or production activities at Molulu and for general working capital.
On 3 July 2026 NIU agreed to subscribed for £2,500,000 of convertible loan notes issued under the 2025 CLN Instrument at par at the following times:
(i)
£1,100,000 on or before 31 December 2026;
(ii)
£1,000,000 on or before 31 May 2027; and
(iii)
£400,000 to applied to repay the sums due under the facility provided to the Company by NIU in July 2025.
The main terms of the 2025 CLN Instrument is as follows:
·
Mature on 18 month from issue of the relevant notes;
·
Interest at 10% per annum, payable on maturity;
·
Are convertible into ordinary shares of the company at a conversation price of 10.25 per Ordinary Share of £0.0005 each in the capital of the Company ("Ordinary Shares"), which is the same conversion price as under the CLN instrument; and
·
May be redeemed at the noteholder's option at any time subject to certain restrictions and will be repayable in cash at the end of the term.
·
There are certain customary events resulting in immediate redemption related to solvency type issues.
The issue of the notes under the 2025 CLN Instrument to NIU is a material related party transaction for the purposes of DTR 7.3.6 due to NIU's shareholding in the Company representing in excess of 60.00% of the issued Ordinary Shares.
Danilo Lange, CEO of Critical Metals, said:
"We are pleased to have secured a further commitment from NIU to provide capital to help us develop the Company's business."
**ENDS**
For further information on the Company please visit
www.criticalmetals.co.uk
or contact:
Critical Metals plc
Danilo Lange, CEO
critical@stbridespartners.co.uk
St Brides Partners Ltd
Financial PR
Ana Ribeiro/Charlotte Page
critical@stbridespartners.co.uk
About Critical Metals
London listed Critical Metals plc is focused on identifying low CAPEX and OPEX brown-field projects with near-term production and cash-flow, concentrating on minerals that have strategic importance to future global economic growth. In line with this, and with an off-take partner already in place, the Company is currently focused on recommencing production at the formerly producing Molulu Copper/Cobalt Project in the Katangan Copperbelt in Democratic Republic of Congo ('DRC').

latest.content:
Today 10:07

Critical Metals PLC
12 May 2026
Critical Metals plc / EPIC: CRTM / Market: Main Market
12 May 2026
Critical Metals Plc
("Critical Metals" or the "Company")
Board Changes
Critical Metals plc (
LSE:CRTM)
, a mining company established to acquire mining opportunities in the critical and strategic metals sector, currently developing the Molulu Copper/Cobalt Project ("Molulu") in the Democratic Republic of Congo, announces the permanent appointment of Mr Danilo Lange as Chief Executive Officer, with immediate effect.
Mr Lange, an experienced international executive with over 25 years of leadership experience across mining, consumer goods, and marketing sectors, had served as the Company's Interim CEO since December 2025.
Kelvin Williams, Non-Executive Chairman, said:
"
We are very pleased that Danilo has agreed to continue as Chief Executive Officer on a permanent basis following his appointment as interim CEO in December 2025. During this period, he has demonstrated a clear understanding of the business. His experience and performance in the role made him the best candidate for the role."
Mr Danilo Lange, CEO of Critical Metals plc, added:
"I am delighted to be appointed as the CEO of Critical Metals on a permanent basis. I would like to take the opportunity to thank the board for their support and look forward to advancing on our stated strategy, to invest in low-capex, close to production projects with exposure to critical metals."
**ENDS**

company_30s.what_they_do: Critical Metals Plc mines and processes critical minerals such as lithium, cobalt and nickel that are essential for batteries, electronics and other high‑tech applications.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The global push for electric vehicles, renewable energy and advanced electronics is driving demand for these metals. Critical Metals is positioned to supply that demand, but it competes with larger, more established miners and faces the risk of supply chain disruptions.
company_30s.current_state: The company has struggled with liquidity and performance, recently suspending trading and filing several RNS reports about debt facilities, board changes and a significant stake takeover by NIU Invest. It is currently operating under tight financial conditions and uncertain trading status.

rns_narrative: The company has been trying to shore up cash by issuing convertible loan notes and welcoming a large shareholding from NIU Invest, signalling a push to stay afloat.
Governance has been in flux: board reshuffles and interim results indicate attempts to stabilize operations, but the interim numbers were weak and the AGM was postponed.
Trading has been halted due to regulatory concerns, raising fears of a delisting or further financial distress.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Cautiously skeptical – investors are wary but not yet convinced the company is doomed.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: No clear bullish story has emerged; any optimism is tied to the possibility of a funding injection from NIU Invest.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Bears point to the trading suspension, weak results, and the fact that the company is still looking for liquidity. They worry that the firm could be delisted or forced into insolvency.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The mood has hardened over the last week: early chatter about a potential turnaround has been eclipsed by reports of suspension and weak earnings.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends shows zero interest – a perfect setup for a surprise move if a catalyst hits.

near_term_catalysts: Re‑opening of trading on the LSE after the suspension is lifted.
A formal announcement of new funding or a strategic partnership that lifts liquidity.
Positive interim or annual results that demonstrate cost control or a new mine discovery.
A volume spike that breaks the current support level on a key chart.
expect_next.watch_for: Monitor the trading resume date, any volume surge above 10× the 20‑day average, and the price breaking the 50‑day moving average. A clear positive earnings release would be a decisive signal.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock appears to be in the early stages of a deep crash – capitulation has likely occurred but no clear recovery has begun. Confirmation will require a sustained move above the current support and a return of volume.

buy_vs_sell.lean: Neutral – the evidence for a bounce is weak and the risks are high.
buy_vs_sell.bull_case: If the company successfully raises capital, lifts its trading, and posts a better-than‑expected earnings report, the stock could recover to pre‑crash levels, offering a 2‑to‑3× return on the current price.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: Without new funding or a positive results announcement, the company risks further liquidity problems, potential delisting, or bankruptcy. The downside could be a 70–80% decline from its all‑time high.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential upside is roughly 2–3× the current price if a recovery occurs, but the downside risk is large – the stock could fall well below the current level if the liquidity crisis deepens. The asymmetry favors the upside only if a clear catalyst emerges.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter only after trading resumes and the price closes above the 50‑day moving average. Use a position size that limits exposure to 5% of your portfolio and set a stop just below the recent low to protect against a false breakout.
playbook.if_watching: Wait for a volume spike of at least 10× the average and a clear earnings announcement. If either occurs, reassess the trade setup immediately.
playbook.if_passing: If the company files for insolvency, is delisted, or the trading suspension is extended beyond 30 days, exit all positions and consider the setup dead.

ai_insights.bottom_line: With no confirmed deep crash, a trading halt, and weak financials, the current risk outweighs the upside unless a decisive funding or earnings catalyst materialises.
